docs.title: Terminate Optimizer Worker Processes
docs.text: This document describes a targeted script for terminating optimizer worker processes. It avoids killing unrelated processes that merely contain the word hyper in their command line.

docs.title: Important safety note
docs.text:
Stop the active optimizer sweep in the dashboard before running the script. Otherwise, the sweep manager may immediately create replacement workers.

The script sends SIGTERM first, waits briefly, and then sends SIGKILL to remaining matching processes. The second signal also removes workers that are stuck in the stopped (T) process state.

Completed optimizer results remain persisted on disk and can be resumed after the dashboard is restarted.

docs.title: Script
docs.text:
Save the following as kill_optimizer_workers.sh:

#!/usr/bin/env bash

# Terminate Python module processes matching PROCESS_SUBJECT.
# The first positional argument takes precedence over the environment variable.
# Example:
#   ./kill_optimizer_workers.sh 'optimizer\.hyperopt_runner'
#   PROCESS_SUBJECT='optimizer\.hyperopt_runner' ./kill_optimizer_workers.sh

set -u

PROCESS_SUBJECT="${1:-${PROCESS_SUBJECT:-optimizer\.hyperopt_runner}}"
PYTHON_EXEC_RE='(^|/)python(3)?$'

optimizer_pids() {
  ps -eo pid=,args= |
    awk -v subject="$PROCESS_SUBJECT" -v python_exec="$PYTHON_EXEC_RE" '
      $2 ~ python_exec &&
      $0 ~ ("(^|[[:space:]])-m[[:space:]]+" subject "([[:space:]]|$)") {
        print $1
      }
    '
}

terminate_processes() {
  local signal="$1"
  local pids

  pids="$(optimizer_pids)"

  if [[ -z "$pids" ]]; then
    echo "No matching optimizer processes found."
    return
  fi

  echo "Sending SIG${signal} to:"
  echo "$pids"

  # PIDs come directly from ps and are numeric.
  kill "-${signal}" $pids 2>/dev/null || true
}

echo "Matching processes before termination:"
optimizer_pids

terminate_processes TERM

# Give normal shutdown a moment to complete.
sleep 2

# Remove workers that did not respond, including stopped (T-state) workers.
terminate_processes KILL

echo
if [[ -z "$(optimizer_pids)" ]]; then
  echo "All matching processes have been removed."
else
  echo "Some matching processes remain:"
  optimizer_pids
fi

docs.title: Usage
docs.text:
Make the script executable:

chmod +x kill_optimizer_workers.sh

Terminate the optimizer workers:

./kill_optimizer_workers.sh

The default target is:

optimizer.hyperopt_runner

To pass a different module without editing the script:

./kill_optimizer_workers.sh 'another\.module_name'

The same value can be supplied through the environment:

PROCESS_SUBJECT='another\.module_name' ./kill_optimizer_workers.sh

The positional argument takes precedence over the environment variable.

docs.title: Why ps -aux | grep hyper | wc -l is unreliable
docs.text:
That command also counts the grep process itself and any unrelated command containing hyper. The script matches the exact Python module invocation:

python -m optimizer.hyperopt_runner

It therefore does not terminate unrelated dashboard, exchange, or test processes.

docs.title: After termination
docs.text: Restart the dashboard so the current optimizer concurrency settings are loaded. Then resume the persisted sweep through the dashboard or the supported /api/optimizer/sweep/resume endpoint.

docs.title: Tailscale – Overall Overview and Recommendations
docs.text:
Based on our discussions, Tailscale looks like a very interesting solution for your infrastructure. It could give you secure remote access to your Linux VMs, WSL2 development environment, web applications and other services without exposing them directly to the internet.

Below is a consolidated overview of what we discussed, including the security considerations and my recommendations.

docs.title: 1. What is Tailscale?
docs.text:
Tailscale is a mesh VPN solution built on top of WireGuard.

It creates a private network between your devices, regardless of their physical location.

For example, you could connect:

  • Windows 11 desktop.
  • Ubuntu running inside WSL2.
  • Remote Linux VMs.
  • Android smartphone.
  • Home Assistant.
  • Docker servers.
  • Other Linux machines.

All these devices become part of your private network.

Each device receives a private Tailscale IP address, generally in the 100.x.x.x range.

You can communicate between devices as if they were connected to the same local network.

Official website: Tailscale

docs.title: 2. How does the network operate?
docs.text:
Tailscale uses WireGuard encryption to establish secure connections.

There are two possible connection methods.

docs.title: A. Direct connection (preferred)
docs.text:
Windows PC
     |
     | WireGuard encrypted
     |
Internet
     |
     | WireGuard encrypted
     |
Linux VM

The traffic travels directly between your devices.

Tailscale's coordination servers help establish the connection but do not carry the actual traffic.

docs.title: B. DERP relay
docs.text:
If a direct connection cannot be established, Tailscale can use a relay server.

Windows PC
     |
     | Encrypted traffic
     |
Tailscale DERP server
     |
     | Encrypted traffic
     |
Linux VM

Even when using a relay, the traffic remains encrypted.

docs.title: Can Tailscale see your data?
docs.text:
Generally, no.

Information Tailscale access SSH passwords No SSH private keys No Terminal contents No Files transferred No HTTP application contents No Device IP addresses Yes Device identities Yes Connection metadata Yes Traffic volume and timing Potentially

There are two independent encryption layers when using SSH:

  1. WireGuard encryption between devices.
  2. SSH encryption between the SSH client and server.

You are still trusting Tailscale's coordination infrastructure to manage device identities and network configuration correctly.

docs.title: 3. Security and vulnerability management
docs.text:
We discussed whether Tailscale is sufficiently secure and how well it manages vulnerabilities.

My assessment is that Tailscale is a mature security-focused product.

However, it is important to distinguish between two things:

What Tailscale protects: - Network communications. - Remote access. - Device authentication. - Unauthorized network connections. - Exposure of services to the public internet.

What Tailscale does not protect: - Vulnerabilities in Linux. - Vulnerable Docker containers. - Vulnerable web applications. - Malware running on your machines. - Compromised Windows installations. - Vulnerabilities in Tailscale itself.

You should therefore maintain normal security practices:

  • Keep Tailscale updated.
  • Enable MFA.
  • Restrict device access.
  • Keep Linux security updates enabled.
  • Use SSH public/private key authentication.
  • Disable SSH password authentication.
  • Disable root SSH login.
  • Apply firewall rules.

Tailscale also publishes security advisories:

Tailscale Security Bulletins

docs.title: 4. Windows 11 versus WSL2 installation
docs.text:
This was one of the more interesting aspects of our discussion.

There are two installation possibilities.

docs.title: Option A: Install Tailscale on Windows
docs.text:
Windows 11
           |
       Tailscale
           |
          WSL2
           |
        Ubuntu
           |
       SSH / HTTP

Advantages: - Simple installation. - All Windows applications can access the Tailscale network. - WSL2 can use the Windows network connection. - Easy integration with VS Code. - No additional VPN installation inside Ubuntu.

Disadvantages: - Installs a privileged Windows service. - Adds a virtual network interface. - Adds another component to your Windows attack surface.

docs.title: Option B: Install Tailscale inside WSL2
docs.text:
Windows 11
           |
          WSL2
           |
        Ubuntu
           |
       Tailscale
           |
       WireGuard
           |
        Internet

Advantages: - No additional Tailscale service on Windows. - Separate Tailscale device identity. - VPN functionality managed by Linux.

Disadvantages: - More complicated networking configuration. - WSL2 networking limitations. - Windows applications do not automatically become Tailscale-connected devices.

My preference, considering your security concerns, is to investigate the WSL2 installation first.

One important qualification: WSL2 is not a complete security boundary. It shares the Windows host's underlying kernel infrastructure.

Also, don't run independent Tailscale installations in Windows and WSL2 simultaneously unless you have a specific reason and understand the networking implications.

Documentation:

Tailscale WSL2 documentation

docs.title: 5. Remote SSH access to Linux
docs.text:
This was your original requirement.

With Tailscale, you can access your Linux VM without exposing SSH to the public internet.

For example:

ssh username@100.x.y.z

You don't need: - Public IP addresses. - Router port forwarding. - Publicly exposed SSH ports. - Dynamic DNS. - An externally accessible SSH server.

I recommend retaining standard OpenSSH rather than using Tailscale SSH.

This means: - Your SSH server remains OpenSSH. - You manage your own SSH keys. - Tailscale only provides private network connectivity. - SSH authentication remains independently managed.

docs.title: 6. Web application development and testing
docs.text:
We also discussed whether Tailscale can be used for web application development.

The answer is yes.

You can access web applications running on any connected machine.

For example, suppose you run a Next.js application on your Linux VM:

npm run dev -- --hostname 0.0.0.0

You can access it from Windows using:

http://100.x.y.z:3000

You can also do the reverse: run applications on Windows and access them remotely from Linux or Android.

Typical applications include:

Application Example Next.js Port 3000 Vite Port 5173 Node.js API Port 8080 Portainer Port 9443 Home Assistant Port 8123 Grafana Port 3000

You should restrict access to trusted devices and avoid exposing development servers unnecessarily.

docs.title: Tailscale Serve
docs.text:
Another interesting feature is Tailscale Serve.

It allows you to expose a local web application to your private Tailscale network using HTTPS.

For example:

tailscale serve --bg 3000

This provides an HTTPS address for accessing your application.

Documentation: Tailscale Serve

docs.title: 7. Android support
docs.text:
Tailscale has an official Android application.

Download:

Tailscale Android – Google Play

You can use it to:

  • SSH into Linux machines.
  • Access web applications.
  • Access Home Assistant.
  • Access Portainer.
  • Access private APIs.
  • Access your development environment.

It works over mobile data and public Wi-Fi.

You simply authenticate using the same Tailscale account.

docs.title: 8. Tailscale versus alternatives
docs.text:
We also discussed WireGuard and OpenVPN.

Here is the comparison:

Feature Tailscale WireGuard OpenVPN Underlying protocol WireGuard WireGuard OpenVPN Encryption Excellent Excellent Excellent Peer-to-peer Yes Yes Depends on configuration Automatic NAT traversal Yes Requires configuration Depends on configuration Central coordination Tailscale Self-managed Self-managed Self-hosting Headscale Yes Yes Configuration complexity Low Medium Medium/high Open source Client components Yes Yes

docs.title: Headscale
docs.text:
We also discussed Headscale.

Headscale is an open-source, self-hosted implementation of the Tailscale coordination server.

Headscale GitHub repository

It offers an interesting alternative if you want to retain the Tailscale client experience while controlling the coordination infrastructure yourself.

docs.title: 9. Proposed architecture
docs.text:
Taking everything into account, this is the architecture I would investigate for your environment:

                       INTERNET
                           |
                    Tailscale Network
                           |
             +-------------+-------------+
             |             |             |
          Windows        Android       Linux VM
           11             Phone        Remote
             |                           |
           WSL2                        OpenSSH
             |                           |
         Development                  Docker
             |                           |
         Node.js /                   Applications
          Next.js                    Portainer
                                      Home Assistant
                                      APIs

The idea is to have a private network connecting your development environment, remote infrastructure and mobile devices.

Your existing OpenVPN installation can remain independent. You don't need to replace it.

docs.title: 10. My final recommendations
docs.text:
Based on our discussions, I would prioritize the following:

Priority Recommendation 1 Use Tailscale for private remote connectivity 2 Investigate installation inside WSL2 3 Retain standard OpenSSH 4 Use SSH keys exclusively 5 Enable MFA 6 Restrict access using Tailscale ACLs/grants 7 Avoid exposing SSH and development ports publicly 8 Keep Linux and Tailscale updated 9 Install Tailscale on Android for mobile access 10 Investigate Headscale if you eventually want self-hosted coordination

docs.title: Overall conclusion
docs.text:
I think Tailscale is a particularly good fit for your requirements.

The three main benefits are:

  1. Security: You eliminate the need to expose SSH and development services directly to the internet.
  2. Convenience: You can access your infrastructure from Windows, WSL2, Linux and Android.
  3. Development: You can develop applications on one machine and test them remotely on another without configuring public networking.

docs.title: Graphene Supercapacitors
docs.text: Graphene supercapacitors are advanced energy‑storage devices that use graphene as the electrode material to dramatically improve the performance of traditional supercapacitors. The core idea: supercapacitors store energy electrostatically, not chemically like batteries — and graphene maximizes the speed, power, and lifetime of this process.

docs.title: ⚡ Short answer
docs.text: A graphene supercapacitor is a high‑power energy storage device that uses graphene’s enormous surface area and conductivity to store electric charge extremely fast, deliver huge bursts of power, and survive millions of cycles — but with lower energy density than batteries. Graphene improves supercapacitors by increasing surface area, ion accessibility, conductivity, and mechanical stability, enabling next‑generation high‑power applications. RSC Publishing eureka.patsnap.com

docs.title: 🧩 How a supercapacitor works (in simple terms)
docs.text:
Supercapacitors store energy in an electric double layer (EDL): - Two electrodes (usually carbon‑based) - An electrolyte with ions - A separator

When voltage is applied, ions accumulate on the electrode surfaces → forming a double layer → storing charge physically, not chemically.

This is why supercapacitors: - Charge in seconds - Deliver very high power - Last millions of cycles - But store less total energy than batteries

docs.title: 🧪 Why graphene makes supercapacitors far better
docs.text: Graphene is a single layer of carbon atoms with extreme properties:

docs.title: 1. Huge surface area → more charge storage
docs.text: Graphene’s theoretical surface area is 2,630 m²/g, far higher than activated carbon (100–200 m²/g). This allows theoretical capacitance up to ~550 F/g, far above conventional materials. eureka.patsnap.com

docs.title: 2. Very high electrical conductivity → fast charging/discharging
docs.text: Pristine graphene conductivity exceeds 1,700 S/m, compared to <10 S/m for activated carbon. This reduces internal resistance (ESR) and boosts power density. eureka.patsnap.com

docs.title: 3. Mechanical strength → long lifetime
docs.text: Graphene’s tensile strength (~130 GPa) and stiffness (Young’s modulus ~1 TPa) prevent structural degradation over millions of cycles. eureka.patsnap.com

docs.title: 4. Tunability through doping and composites
docs.text:
Graphene can be combined with: - Metal oxides (MOs) - Transition metal dichalcogenides (TMDs) - Heteroatom doping (N, B, S)

These improve ion diffusion, charge transport, and energy density. RSC Publishing

docs.title: 🔋 Types of graphene supercapacitors
docs.text: Graphene can be used in several architectures:

docs.title: 1. Electric Double‑Layer Capacitors (EDLCs)
docs.text: Pure graphene or graphene‑derived carbon. - Highest power - Fastest charge - Longest cycle life RSC Publishing

docs.title: 2. Pseudocapacitors
docs.text: Graphene + metal oxides (MnO₂, RuO₂) or conductive polymers. - Higher energy density - Slightly lower cycle life RSC Publishing

docs.title: 3. Asymmetric supercapacitors (ASC)
docs.text: Graphene negative electrode + pseudocapacitive positive electrode. - Balanced energy + power RSC Publishing

docs.title: 🚀 Performance advantages
docs.text: Feature Graphene Supercapacitor Conventional Supercapacitor Energy density Higher (due to SSA & composites) Lower Power density Extremely high High Charge time Seconds Seconds Cycle life Millions Millions Conductivity Very high Moderate Heat generation Very low Low

docs.title: 🔧 Where graphene supercapacitors are used
docs.text:
Graphene supercapacitors are ideal for high‑power, fast‑charge applications:

  • Regenerative braking in EVs
  • Bus/tram acceleration systems
  • Grid buffering for renewables
  • Industrial cranes/elevators
  • UPS systems
  • High‑power electronics
  • Wearable/flexible electronics (future)

Skeleton Technologies (Estonia) is a leading commercial developer using curved graphene to boost performance. youtube.com youtube.com

docs.title: 🧱 Limitations
docs.text: Even with graphene, supercapacitors still have lower energy density than lithium batteries. Research focuses on: - Doping - Composite formation - 3D graphene aerogels - Hybrid battery‑capacitor systems RSC Publishing

docs.title: 🧭 Bottom line
docs.text:
Graphene supercapacitors are not a battery replacement yet, but they are a revolution in high‑power energy storage. They excel at: - Fast charging - High power bursts - Long lifetime - High efficiency

And graphene is the key material enabling the next leap in performance.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: A phase-change battery (PCM thermal battery) stores heat by melting and solidifying a special material. During this phase transition, the material absorbs or releases large amounts of energy at a constant temperature, enabling compact and stable thermal storage.

docs.title: Charging (Heat Absorption)
docs.text: A heat source—typically a heat pump or PV-powered electric element—heats the phase-change material (PCM) to its melting point. As the PCM melts, it absorbs a large amount of latent heat without increasing in temperature.

docs.title: Storage
docs.text: Once melted, the PCM remains in a liquid state as long as its temperature stays above the melting point. Because latent heat storage is highly efficient, PCM modules can store much more energy per liter than water.

docs.title: Discharging (Heat Release)
docs.text: When heat is needed, the PCM cools and solidifies. During solidification, it releases the stored latent heat at a constant temperature, making it ideal for domestic hot water and low-temperature heating systems.

docs.title: Why PCM Is Better Than a Traditional Water Buffer
docs.text:
• High energy density: PCM stores 3–5× more energy per liter than water.
  • Constant output temperature: PCM maintains a fixed temperature (e.g., 55°C) during discharge.
  • Compact design: A 50-liter PCM module can replace a 200-liter water tank.
  • Perfect for PV integration: Excess solar power can be converted into stored heat efficiently.
  • Reduced peak electrical load: Heat pumps can operate when COP is highest, lowering grid demand.

docs.title: Typical Home Integration
docs.text: A PCM battery is usually a compact module (30–80 liters) connected to a heat pump or electric heater. It provides thermal storage for domestic hot water or heating and can be controlled by smart home systems.

docs.title: Example: PCM at 55°C
docs.text:
• Melting point: 55°C
  • Storage capacity: 3–6 kWh per 50 liters
  • Applications: Domestic hot water, low-temperature heating

docs.title: Summary
docs.text: A phase-change battery stores heat by melting and solidifying a special material, enabling compact, efficient, and stable thermal energy storage—ideal for modern heat pumps and solar-powered homes.

docs.title: E-Cat by Andrea Rossi – Video Summary and Critical Assessment
E-Cat by Andrea Rossi – Video Summary and Critical Assessment
docs.text:
The video presents the story of Andrea Rossi's E-Cat (Energy Catalyzer), a device that supposedly produces enormous amounts of energy without conventional fuel, initially through a claimed nuclear process and, in its latest incarnation, by harvesting zero-point energy.

The central question is whether Rossi has actually developed a revolutionary energy source or whether the technology remains an unverified claim.

My assessment: The E-Cat is an interesting technological claim, but there is currently insufficient independently verified evidence to establish that it works as advertised.

Below is a structured summary of the 12-minute video.

docs.title: 1. What is the E-Cat?
docs.text:
Andrea Rossi, born in Milan in 1950, developed the E-Cat together with physicist Sergio Focardi.

Their original concept was based on a phenomenon called Low Energy Nuclear Reactions (LENR), commonly associated with cold fusion.

The original reactor consisted of:

  • A sealed steel chamber.
  • Nickel powder.
  • Hydrogen gas under pressure.
  • Electric heating elements.
  • A supposedly secret catalyst.

The proposed process was:

  1. Hydrogen enters the nickel crystal lattice.
  2. Hydrogen becomes compressed within the metal structure.
  3. Under the influence of a catalyst, Rossi claims that hydrogen nuclei interact with nickel nuclei.
  4. Nickel supposedly transforms into copper.
  5. The nuclear reaction releases substantial heat.

The claimed energy density was extraordinary: approximately 2,000 kWh of heat from one gram of nickel.

This would represent an enormous improvement over conventional chemical energy sources.

docs.title: 2. The development timeline
docs.text:
The video describes several generations of E-Cat technology.

Year Development Main claim 2007 Collaboration with Sergio Focardi Development of nickel-hydrogen reactor 2011 First public demonstration in Bologna Approximately 10 kW thermal output 2011 1 MW container demonstration Approximately 479 kW average output 2012 Proposed domestic E-Cat 10 kW unit for $400–500 2013 Industrial E-Cat Pre-orders around $1.5 million 2017 E-Cat QX Miniature reactor with plasma exceeding 2,600°C 2021 E-Cat SKL Development of direct electrical generation 2023 Live demonstration Small cell powering a motorcycle headlight 2024 Electric vehicle demonstration E-Cat-equipped vehicle reportedly travelled 201 km 2026 Updated NGU technology Approximately 20 units reportedly undergoing long-duration testing

An important distinction: these are developments and performance claims reported in the video, not independently established technical milestones.

docs.title: 3. The transition to direct electricity generation
docs.text:
This is arguably the most interesting part of the video.

Rossi initially concentrated on generating heat.

However, converting heat into electricity introduces significant efficiency losses.

He subsequently pursued a technology capable of generating electricity directly.

The latest device is called the E-Cat NGU (Never Give Up).

According to Rossi, its operating principle is fundamentally different from the original nickel-hydrogen reactor.

docs.title: The proposed mechanism
docs.text:
The video describes:

  • Two metal electrodes.
  • A sealed gap between the electrodes.
  • Plasma containing hydrogen and metal.
  • Extremely dense electron clusters.
  • Interaction with the quantum vacuum.

Rossi claims that these electron clusters interact with the zero-point energy field.

The claimed result is approximately 10 watts of continuous DC electricity per cell.

Importantly, the NGU is presented as requiring no conventional fuel.

This is a very different theoretical proposition from the original nickel-hydrogen E-Cat.

docs.title: 4. The electric car demonstration (September 2024)
docs.text:
This is probably the most spectacular demonstration presented in the video.

Two identical electric cars participated in a test at a racetrack in Latina, Italy.

According to the video:

Parameter Standard car E-Cat car Initial battery charge 96% 62% Distance travelled 73 km 201 km Driving duration 2h 20m More than 6h Final battery charge Empty 83%

The E-Cat vehicle reportedly carried:

  • Its normal 6 kWh battery.
  • An E-Cat assembly.
  • Control electronics.

The proposed operating principle was straightforward:

The E-Cat supplies electricity to the battery while the electric motor consumes electricity.

If the E-Cat produces more electricity than the vehicle consumes, the battery charges while driving.

According to the video, the E-Cat-equipped vehicle finished with a higher battery charge than when it started.

However, this demonstration has not established that the E-Cat generated the claimed energy independently of other energy sources.

To establish that, an independently controlled test would need to measure all electrical inputs and outputs, including battery energy, over a sufficiently long period.

docs.title: 5. What would an E-Cat cost?
docs.text:
The video provides some indicative figures.

Parameter Claimed value Power per module 100 W Estimated module price $250 Expected operating lifetime 100,000 hours Energy production 10,000 kWh Cost per kWh $0.025

The video estimates that an average household would need approximately 12 modules.

That would give:

  • 1.2 kW continuous output.
  • Approximately $3,000 initial investment.
  • More than 11 years of continuous operation.

An inverter and battery would also be required.

These calculations are mathematically consistent with the stated assumptions, but the assumptions themselves have not been independently validated.

docs.title: 6. Why isn't the E-Cat commercially available?
docs.text: This is where the story becomes particularly interesting.

docs.title: The Industrial Heat dispute
docs.text:
In 2012–2013, American investment company Industrial Heat licensed Rossi's technology.

The reported financial arrangement involved:

  • $11.5 million paid initially.
  • Another $89 million conditional on successful testing.

A 350-day test of a 1 MW installation was conducted in Florida.

Rossi claimed that the reactor produced approximately 50 times more energy than it consumed.

Industrial Heat disputed the results and stated that it could not independently confirm the claimed performance.

The dispute eventually went to court.

In July 2017, both parties walked away without the additional payment being made.

This is a significant episode because it involved substantial financial investment and an extended attempt to validate the technology.

docs.title: 7. What does the scientific community say?
docs.text:
This is the most important section of the video.

There are several fundamental problems.

docs.title: A. Independent reproducibility
docs.text:
No independent laboratory has convincingly reproduced Rossi's claimed results under conditions where Rossi does not control the experiment.

For a revolutionary energy technology, independent reproducibility is essential.

docs.title: B. Energy measurements
docs.text:
Some of the earlier demonstrations were criticised because of possible errors in measuring electrical input and thermal output.

For example:

  • Incorrect electrical power measurements.
  • Inadequate accounting for stored thermal energy.
  • Inaccurate water-flow measurements.
  • Insufficient control of experimental conditions.

Even relatively small measurement errors can produce apparently spectacular energy gains.

docs.title: C. Zero-point energy
docs.text:
The latest NGU technology introduces an even more fundamental scientific question.

Zero-point energy is a genuine concept in quantum mechanics.

Even an ideal vacuum has quantum fluctuations and a non-zero ground-state energy.

However, the existence of zero-point energy does not mean that it can be extracted as a continuous, usable energy source.

No established physical mechanism currently demonstrates how the E-Cat could achieve what Rossi claims.

docs.title: 8. My technical assessment
docs.text:
I would separate Rossi's claims into three categories.

Claim Scientific assessment Nickel-hydrogen LENR reactions An area of scientific investigation, but Rossi's claimed performance remains unverified Direct electrical generation Extraordinary claim without convincing independent validation Harvesting zero-point energy No established mechanism demonstrating practical continuous energy extraction 100,000-hour lifetime Requires long-duration independent testing E-Cat-powered electric vehicle Requires independently verified energy accounting

There is an important distinction between the original E-Cat and the latest NGU.

The original technology at least proposed a nuclear reaction involving nickel and hydrogen.

The NGU introduces a fundamentally different explanation involving electron clusters and zero-point energy.

These should not be treated as the same technology simply because Rossi uses the E-Cat name.

docs.title: 9. What happens next?
docs.text:
The video ends with Rossi claiming that:

  • Approximately 20 updated units are undergoing long-duration testing.
  • A worldwide public presentation is planned for January 2027.
  • Deliveries to pre-order customers should follow.

There is an important historical caveat here.

Rossi has announced commercialisation dates and demonstrations before, with dates subsequently postponed.

The decisive evidence will be whether independent customers receive functioning units and can operate them without hidden energy inputs.

docs.title: 10. My conclusion: Is Andrea Rossi onto something?
docs.text:
I find three aspects particularly important.

1. The original LENR research

Low-energy nuclear reactions have been investigated by various researchers for decades. The field is controversial, but it is legitimate to investigate anomalous experimental results.

However, that does not validate Rossi's particular reactor.

2. The transition to zero-point energy

This is where I become considerably more sceptical.

Quantum vacuum fluctuations are real, but extracting usable continuous energy from the vacuum would represent a major breakthrough in fundamental physics.

Rossi has not provided independently verified evidence establishing such a mechanism.

3. The electric car demonstration

This is potentially the most interesting claim because it should be relatively straightforward to verify.

An independent laboratory could install the device in an electric vehicle and measure:

  • Initial and final battery energy.
  • All electrical inputs.
  • Electrical output from the E-Cat.
  • Energy consumed by the motor.
  • Operating conditions and measurement uncertainty.

A sufficiently long, independently monitored test would settle much of the controversy.

docs.title: 11. What I would consider convincing evidence
docs.text:
If I were evaluating the E-Cat as a potential investment or technology, I would insist on five things:

  1. Independent testing: A recognised laboratory conducts the experiment without Rossi controlling the measurements.
  2. Transparent instrumentation: Complete electrical schematics, calibrated meters and publicly available measurement data.
  3. Long-duration operation: At least several months of continuous operation.
  4. Energy balance: Demonstration that total electrical output substantially exceeds every possible energy input.
  5. Commercial deployment: Actual customers operate the technology independently and publish verifiable results.

Until then, I would not consider the E-Cat a commercially demonstrated energy technology.

docs.title: Final verdict
docs.text:
The video is an interesting introduction to Andrea Rossi's claims, but it is somewhat promotional in its presentation.

It describes spectacular demonstrations without adequately explaining the methodological criticisms or providing independent experimental evidence.

My position: intriguing claims, extraordinary potential, but insufficient scientific evidence.

The January 2027 presentation mentioned in the video could be an important milestone. However, another demonstration controlled by Rossi would not resolve the fundamental question.

What matters is independent, reproducible measurement of the complete energy balance.

*Source: E-Cat by Andrea Rossi – Video Summary and Critical Assessment

docs.title: modular 48V LiFePO4 home backup system
docs.text:
Excellent. I would build this as a modular 48V LiFePO4 home backup system, inspired by Will Prowse's design, but adapted to European electrical standards and Belgian regulations.

The idea is to start with approximately 10kWh of battery storage, have automatic switching when the electricity fails, and make it possible to expand to 20–30kWh without replacing the original equipment.

I would also prepare the installation for solar panels at a later stage, even though we won't install them initially.

docs.title: 1. Proposed system architecture
docs.text:
My recommendation is to use components from Victron Energy and Pylontech.

Why?

  • Modular architecture.
  • Good compatibility between inverter and batteries.
  • Excellent monitoring capabilities.
  • Expandable battery capacity.
  • European 230V/50Hz equipment.
  • Established ecosystem and technical documentation.

Here is the architecture I propose:

docs.title: Electrical architecture
docs.text:
BELGIAN ELECTRICITY GRID

                       BATTERY BUSBAR

The important feature is that the inverter acts as both:

  1. An inverter, converting battery DC into 230V AC.
  2. A battery charger, charging the batteries from the electricity grid.

It also contains an automatic transfer switch.

When the grid fails, the inverter switches to battery operation.

When the grid returns, it switches back and can recharge the batteries.

This is precisely what we want.

docs.title: 2. Battery storage: approximately 10kWh
docs.text: I recommend starting with two Pylontech US5000 batteries.

docs.title: Pylontech US5000
docs.text:
Technical specifications:

Specification Value Battery chemistry LiFePO4 Nominal voltage 48V Capacity 100Ah Energy 4.8kWh Usable energy 4.56kWh Continuous charge/discharge 100A Maximum discharge 120A for 15 minutes Weight 39.7kg Communication CAN / RS485 Cycle life >8,000 cycles

Source: Pylontech manufacturer specifications. en.pylontech.com.cn

Two batteries provide:

Configuration Capacity Battery 1 4.8kWh Battery 2 4.8kWh Total nominal 9.6kWh Total usable 9.12kWh

This is a good starting point.

docs.title: Future expansion
docs.text:
One advantage of this system is that you can add more batteries.

Number of batteries Nominal capacity Usable capacity 2 9.6kWh 9.12kWh 3 14.4kWh 13.68kWh 4 19.2kWh 18.24kWh 5 24kWh 22.8kWh 6 28.8kWh 27.36kWh

Pylontech specifies support for up to 16 modules in a single string, subject to the installation requirements.

My suggestion is to install a battery rack that can accommodate at least six batteries from the beginning.

That avoids rebuilding the installation later.

docs.title: 3. Inverter: Victron MultiPlus-II
docs.text:
This is the central component.

I recommend:

Victron MultiPlus-II 48/5000/70-50 230V

Specifications:

Specification Value Battery voltage 48V AC output 230V Frequency 50Hz Apparent power 5000VA Continuous active power 4000W Peak power 9000W Battery charging current 70A Automatic transfer switch 50A Maximum efficiency 96%

Source: Victron technical documentation. Victron Energy

Notice something important:

Although it is advertised as a 5000VA inverter, its continuous real power output is 4000W at 25°C.

That is still sufficient for many essential household appliances.

docs.title: Why this inverter?
docs.text:
It provides:

  • Automatic switching during a power failure.
  • Battery charging from the electricity grid.
  • Pure sine-wave output.
  • Configurable charging parameters.
  • Remote monitoring.
  • Possibility of adding solar charging equipment later.

It also supports parallel operation and more advanced system configurations.

One important Belgian consideration: the exact model, firmware and grid-connected configuration must be checked against the applicable Synergrid requirements before purchase.

docs.title: 4. Monitoring: Victron Cerbo GX
docs.text:
I would add a Cerbo GX.

This allows you to monitor the complete installation.

You can see:

  • Battery state of charge.
  • Remaining battery capacity.
  • Battery voltage.
  • Charging current.
  • Inverter power consumption.
  • AC input power.
  • AC output power.
  • System alarms.

You can access the information through Victron's VRM monitoring portal.

This is particularly useful when you are away from home.

You could, for example, check whether your battery is fully charged before a forecasted storm.

The Cerbo GX also provides integration possibilities with Home Assistant.

Given your existing Home Assistant and Node-RED environment, this is something I would definitely implement.

docs.title: 5. Battery rack and electrical protection
docs.text:
I would not mount the components on a hand truck for a permanent home installation.

Instead, I would use a metal battery rack.

Recommended configuration:

  • Six-battery-capacity rack.
  • Two batteries initially.
  • Room for four additional batteries.
  • Inverter mounted separately.
  • Proper ventilation.
  • Protected DC distribution.
  • Accessible emergency isolation.

docs.title: Protection components
docs.text:
You will need:

Component Purpose DC battery fuse Protects battery cables DC isolator Disconnects battery system DC busbars Distributes battery current Battery communication cables BMS communication AC input breaker Protects grid input AC output protection Protects backup circuits RCD protection Residual-current protection Earthing system Electrical safety Enclosure Protects electrical components

The exact fuse ratings, cable cross-sections, earthing arrangement and RCD configuration must be calculated for the final installation.

I would have a qualified Belgian electrician design and commission the electrical connections.

docs.title: 6. How much backup electricity will you have?
docs.text:
Let's assume you have 9.12kWh of usable battery energy.

Allowing approximately 10% conversion losses, you have around 8.2kWh available to your appliances.

Some examples:

Average consumption Approximate backup time 200W 41 hours 300W 27 hours 500W 16 hours 750W 11 hours 1000W 8 hours 1500W 5.5 hours 2000W 4 hours

These are theoretical estimates assuming a relatively constant load.

Actual performance depends on inverter consumption, battery temperature, load peaks and the appliances being powered.

docs.title: What could you power?
docs.text:
For example:

Appliance Typical consumption Refrigerator 100–200W average Freezer 50–100W average Internet router 10–20W LED lighting 30–100W Television 80–150W Laptop 50–100W Desktop computer 150–400W Circulation pump 50–150W

You should be able to run essential household equipment quite comfortably.

However, I would not initially include electric heating, electric boilers, induction cooking or EV charging in the backup circuit.

docs.title: 7. Estimated component costs
docs.text:
Here is an initial shopping budget based on currently available European retail listings.

These are indicative prices, not installation quotations.

Estimated hardware total: €3,630–4,970.

This excludes installation, inspection and any necessary modifications to your existing electrical distribution board.

docs.title: 8. Preparing for solar panels later
docs.text:
Although we aren't installing solar panels initially, I would design the installation with solar expansion in mind.

The future architecture would look like this:

                 SOLAR PANELS
                      |
                      |
                DC DISCONNECT
                      |
                      |
                 MPPT CONTROLLER
                      |
                      |
                      v
              +---------------+
              |               |
              |  48V BATTERY  |
              |               |
              +-------+-------+
                      |
                      |
                VICTRON INVERTER
                      |
                      |
                  230V OUTPUT
                      |
                      |
                HOUSEHOLD LOADS

This means you won't need to replace the original batteries or inverter.

You simply add the solar panels, MPPT controller and associated protection.

An alternative is to use a compatible AC-coupled solar inverter, depending on the final system design.

docs.title: 9. Belgian installation requirements
docs.text:
There is an important distinction between a completely isolated backup installation and an inverter/charger that remains connected to the public electricity network.

Even if you intend to use the batteries only during power failures, the installation topology matters.

For Belgium:

  1. The installation must comply with AREI.
  2. Grid-connected inverter equipment must meet applicable Synergrid requirements.
  3. The appropriate installation and inspection requirements must be followed.
  4. Registration with Fluvius may be required for the storage installation.

Check the official resources:

  • Synergrid C10/26 equipment list
  • Fluvius battery information
  • Victron MultiPlus-II technical documentation

I would specifically ask the installer to confirm that the proposed MultiPlus-II configuration is permitted in Belgium before ordering the equipment.

docs.title: 10. Three things I would like to establish before finalising the design
docs.text: There are three technical details that could significantly change the design and cost.

docs.title: A. Single-phase or three-phase electricity?
docs.text:
This is particularly important in Belgium.

Do you have:

  • 230V single-phase?
  • 3 × 230V?
  • 3 × 400V + N?

You can find this on your electricity meter or electricity installation documentation.

A single 48V MultiPlus-II provides single-phase 230V output. It does not independently provide a complete three-phase backup supply.

docs.title: B. What should happen during a power failure?
docs.text:
My preferred solution is to have a dedicated backup distribution board.

For example:

Circuit Backup Refrigerator/freezer Yes Lighting Yes Internet/network Yes Television Yes Computer Yes General sockets Selected Washing machine Optional Dishwasher No Electric heating No EV charger No

Alternatively, we can investigate backing up the entire house, but this requires more careful power and phase calculations.

docs.title: C. Where will you install the batteries?
docs.text:
• Garage
  • Basement
  • Technical room
  • Utility room

This affects the battery enclosure, temperature requirements, cable routing and installation costs.

docs.title: My preferred starting configuration
docs.text:
If the electrical supply allows it, I would start with:

Component Configuration Battery 2 × Pylontech US5000 Storage 9.6kWh nominal Inverter Victron MultiPlus-II 48/5000 Monitoring Cerbo GX Battery rack Six-battery capacity Backup Dedicated essential-circuits distribution board Solar Prepared for future installation

The goal: Build a system once, start with approximately 10kWh, and expand to nearly 30kWh simply by adding batteries.

The most important question now is whether your home has single-phase or three-phase electricity. That determines which inverter architecture I would choose.

docs.title: BPC 157
docs.text:
BPC-157 (Body Protection Compound-157) is een synthetisch peptide van 15 aminozuren. Het is gebaseerd op een stukje van een beschermend eiwit dat van nature in maagsap voorkomt.

Het wordt vooral onderzocht en gebruikt in de “research peptide”-wereld vanwege mogelijke effecten op herstel en bescherming van weefsels.

docs.title: Wat wordt erover beweerd?
docs.text:
In dierstudies (vooral ratten) laat het vaak sterke resultaten zien bij: - Versneld herstel van wonden, spieren, pezen, banden en botten - Bescherming van de darmen (maagzweren, ontstekingen, “leaky gut”) - Ontstekingsremming - Aanmaak van nieuwe bloedvaatjes (wat herstel kan helpen)

Veel gebruikers (op forums en in biohackingkringen) rapporteren anekdotisch sneller herstel van blessures, minder darmklachten of minder pijn. Het wordt soms gecombineerd met andere peptiden zoals TB-500.

docs.title: Wat zegt de wetenschap bij mensen?
docs.text: Het bewijs bij mensen is zeer beperkt. Er zijn bijna geen grote, goed opgezette studies (geen grote gerandomiseerde trials). De meeste kennis komt uit dieronderzoek en persoonlijke verhalen. Het is daarom nog niet bewezen dat het bij mensen even goed of veilig werkt.

docs.title: Belangrijke status
docs.text:
• Het is geen goedgekeurd medicijn (niet door de EMA, FDA of Nederlandse autoriteiten voor menselijk gebruik).
  • Het wordt verkocht als “research chemical”, vaak om te injecteren (onder de huid) of in capsulevorm.
  • De kwaliteit van producten die je online koopt is vaak onzeker (verontreinigingen, verkeerde dosering, onbekende zuiverheid).
  • Lange-termijnveiligheid bij mensen is onvoldoende onderzocht. Theoretische aandachtspunten zijn onder andere effecten op bloedvatgroei (relevant bij bestaande tumoren) en mogelijke immuunreacties.

Het verschilt sterk van goedgekeurde peptide-medicijnen zoals insuline of GLP-1-middelen (Ozempic e.d.), die uitgebreid getest zijn. Het lijkt meer op GHK-Cu in de zin dat het om herstel gaat, maar BPC-157 heeft veel minder humaan bewijs en wordt meestal niet topicaal (op de huid) gebruikt.

Kortom: BPC-157 is een experimenteel peptide met veelbelovende resultaten in dieren, vooral voor weefselherstel en darmen. Bij mensen is het onbewezen en niet goedgekeurd. Zelf gebruiken (vooral injecteren van ongereguleerde producten) brengt risico’s met zich mee.

Dit is algemene informatie, geen medisch advies en geen aanmoediging tot gebruik. Als je blessures, darmklachten of andere gezondheidsproblemen hebt: ga naar je huisarts of specialist. Zij kunnen bewezen behandelingen bieden. Experimenteren met research peptides is niet hetzelfde als een veilige, gecontroleerde behandeling.

docs.title: GHK Cu
docs.text:
GHK-Cu (ook wel kopertripeptide of copper peptide genoemd) is een klein, natuurlijk peptide van drie aminozuren (glycine-histidine-lysine) dat koper bindt. Het komt van nature voor in je lichaam (in bloedplasma, speeksel en urine). De hoeveelheid daalt naarmate je ouder wordt.

Het werkt als een signaalstof die cellen aanzet tot herstel. Het stimuleert onder andere de aanmaak van collageen en elastine (voor stevigheid van de huid), helpt bij wondgenezing, heeft een ontstekingsremmende werking en werkt als antioxidant.

docs.title: Hoe wordt het gebruikt?
docs.text:
Het wordt vooral topicaal (op de huid) toegepast, in crèmes, serums en lotions. Dat is de meest gebruikelijke en best onderzochte manier.

Mensen gebruiken het voor: - Stevigere, gladdere huid en minder zichtbare rimpels - Betere huidtextuur en herstel (bijvoorbeeld na beschadiging of bij littekens) - Soms voor haar (iets meer volume of dikte, al is het bewijs hiervoor beperkter)

Het is een van de oudere en relatief beter onderzochte peptiden in de huidverzorging (al sinds de jaren 70 bekend). Je vindt het in veel cosmetische producten.

Het is niet hetzelfde als de injectiemedicijnen zoals insuline of de GLP-1-spuitjes (Ozempic e.d.). Die werken intern op hormonen en stofwisseling. GHK-Cu is vooral een huidverzorgingspeptide.

docs.title: Realistische verwachtingen
docs.text:
Bij regelmatig gebruik op de huid zien veel mensen geleidelijk een verbetering in stevigheid, hydratatie en uitstraling. Het is geen wondermiddel en de resultaten zijn meestal subtiel tot matig, niet dramatisch. Het werkt het best als onderdeel van een goede huidverzorgingsroutine (reinigen, hydrateren, zonbescherming).

Er is redelijk bewijs voor huidverbetering bij uitwendig gebruik. Claims over sterke interne effecten (via pillen of injecties) zijn veel minder onderbouwd en die vormen worden meestal niet als standaardbehandeling gezien.

Belangrijk: GHK-Cu in crèmes is over het algemeen veilig. Slikken of injecteren zonder medische begeleiding is iets anders en niet aan te raden. Online “research peptides” hebben vaak geen goede kwaliteitscontrole.

Kortom: GHK-Cu is een natuurlijk koperpeptide dat vooral in huidproducten zit om herstel en collageenaanmaak te ondersteunen. Het past bij cosmetische huidverbetering, niet bij de behandeling van interne ziekten zoals diabetes.

Dit is algemene informatie, geen medisch of cosmetisch advies. Bij twijfel of als je het wilt gebruiken: overleg met een huidarts of je huisarts, vooral als je een huidaandoening hebt of andere producten/medicijnen gebruikt.

docs.title: SS 31
docs.text:
SS-31 (ook bekend als elamipretide) is een klein synthetisch peptide van vier aminozuren. Het is speciaal ontworpen om naar de mitochondriën te gaan — de energiefabriekjes in je cellen.

Het bindt daar aan een vetachtige stof (cardiolipine) in de binnenste membraan van de mitochondriën. Daardoor helpt het de energieproductie (ATP) te verbeteren, schadelijke oxidatieve stress te verminderen en de mitochondriën te beschermen tegen schade.

docs.title: Waar wordt het voor onderzocht?
docs.text:
Het is vooral bedoeld voor aandoeningen waarbij de mitochondriën niet goed werken, zoals: - Bepaalde zeldzame mitochondriale ziekten (bijvoorbeeld Barth-syndroom, dat hart en spieren aantast) - Hartfalen of schade na een hartinfarct - Andere aandoeningen met mitochondriale dysfunctie (spierziekten, nier, oog, etc.)

Er zijn klinische studies (fase 2/3) mee gedaan. Sommige lieten positieve signalen zien bij specifieke groepen, andere haalden hun hoofddoelen niet. Het is serieuzer onderzocht dan peptiden zoals BPC-157 of TB-500.

docs.title: Status
docs.text:
Het is geen breed goedgekeurd medicijn voor algemeen gebruik. Het heeft weesgeneesmiddel-status gekregen voor bepaalde zeldzame ziekten en is in ontwikkeling geweest, maar het is geen standaardbehandeling die je zomaar krijgt. Het wordt niet (of nauwelijks) als “research peptide” verkocht zoals BPC-157.

Het verschilt van: - GHK-Cu (vooral huid) - BPC-157 en TB-500 (experimentele herstelpeptiden) - De goedgekeurde peptide-medicijnen zoals insuline of GLP-1-middelen

Kortom: SS-31 is een mitochondriaal beschermend peptide dat in onderzoek zit voor ziekten waarbij de energiehuishouding van cellen verstoord is. Het is geen bewezen, algemeen verkrijgbaar middel voor “meer energie” of anti-aging.

Dit is algemene informatie, geen medisch advies. Bij vermoeidheid, spierklachten of andere gezondheidsproblemen: ga naar je huisarts. Die kan gerichte onderzoeken doen en bewezen behandelingen inzetten. Zelf experimenteren met ongereguleerde peptiden is niet verstandig.

docs.title: TB 500
docs.text:
TB-500 is een synthetisch peptide. Het is een kort fragment van Thymosine Beta-4 (Tβ4), een eiwit dat van nature in je lichaam voorkomt (onder andere in de thymus en veel andere weefsels).

Thymosine Beta-4 speelt een rol bij celbeweging, wondgenezing, het vormen van nieuwe bloedvaatjes en het remmen van ontstekingen. TB-500 bootst een deel van die werking na, vooral het deel dat te maken heeft met herstel van weefsel.

docs.title: Wat wordt erover beweerd?
docs.text:
Het wordt vooral in de “research peptide”-wereld gebruikt en vaak samen met BPC-157. Claims (vooral gebaseerd op dierstudies) gaan over: - Sneller herstel van spieren, pezen, banden en wonden - Minder ontsteking - Betere weefselreparatie

Gebruikers rapporteren anekdotisch sneller herstel van blessures. Het wordt meestal geïnjecteerd (onder de huid of in de spier).

docs.title: Wat zegt de wetenschap bij mensen?
docs.text: Het bewijs bij mensen is zeer beperkt. Er zijn wat vroege studies met het volledige Thymosine Beta-4 (niet altijd met dit korte fragment TB-500) bij wondgenezing of andere toepassingen, maar geen grote, overtuigende onderzoeken die het als standaardbehandeling ondersteunen. De meeste positieve resultaten komen uit dieronderzoek.

docs.title: Belangrijke status
docs.text:
• Het is geen goedgekeurd medicijn voor menselijk gebruik.
  • Het wordt verkocht als research chemical. De kwaliteit, zuiverheid en dosering van producten die je online koopt zijn vaak onzeker.
  • Lange-termijnveiligheid bij mensen is onvoldoende bekend. Mogelijke aandachtspunten zijn onder andere effecten op bloedvatgroei en celgroei (theoretisch relevant bij bestaande tumoren).
  • In de sport is het (net als verwante stoffen) verboden.

Het lijkt in gebruik en status sterk op BPC-157: experimenteel, vooral dierenstudies + anekdotes, geen goedgekeurde behandeling. Het is iets anders dan GHK-Cu (dat vooral in huidcrèmes zit) of de echte peptide-medicijnen zoals insuline of GLP-1-middelen.

Kortom: TB-500 is een experimenteel herstelpeptide, afgeleid van een natuurlijk eiwit, met veelbelovende resultaten in dieren voor weefselherstel. Bij mensen is het onbewezen en niet goedgekeurd. Zelf injecteren van ongereguleerde producten brengt risico’s met zich mee (kwaliteit, onbekende effecten, geen medische controle).

Dit is algemene informatie, geen medisch advies en geen aanmoediging tot gebruik. Bij blessures of herstelproblemen: ga naar je huisarts, fysiotherapeut of specialist. Zij werken met bewezen methoden. Experimenteren met research peptides is geen vervanging voor veilige, gecontroleerde zorg.

docs.title: Wat zijn peptides
docs.text: Peptiden zijn korte ketens van aminozuren (de bouwstenen van eiwitten). Eiwitten zijn lange ketens, peptiden zijn korte stukjes (meestal 2 tot ongeveer 50 aminozuren). Ze werken in je lichaam als boodschappers: ze geven cellen opdrachten, zoals “maak insuline”, “voel je vol” of “bouw bot op”.

docs.title: Hoe worden ze gebruikt om de gezondheid te verbeteren?
docs.text:
Artsen gebruiken nagebootste of aangepaste versies van deze natuurlijke boodschappers als medicijnen (peptide-medicijnen). Die medicijnen zijn meestal injecties, omdat ze in de maag worden afgebroken. Ze zijn op recept verkrijgbaar en worden onder begeleiding van een arts gebruikt.

De bekendste voorbeelden:

  • Insuline – Het bekendste peptide-medicijn. Mensen met diabetes spuiten het om suiker uit het bloed in de cellen te krijgen. Het redt levens en voorkomt complicaties.

  • GLP-1-medicijnen (zoals semaglutide/Ozempic/Wegovy of tirzepatide/Mounjaro) – Dit zijn de bekende “spuitjes” voor diabetes type 2 en overgewicht. Ze bootsen een darmhormoon na en doen onder andere dit:

  • Je voelt je sneller vol en hebt minder trek.
  • De maag loopt langzamer leeg.
  • De alvleesklier maakt beter insuline aan als dat nodig is.
  • Bloedsuiker daalt.
  • Veel mensen vallen aanzienlijk af.
  • Ze beschermen vaak ook het hart en de bloedvaten.

Andere goedgekeurde toepassingen (minder bekend bij het grote publiek): - Medicijnen die botopbouw stimuleren bij botontkalking (osteoporose). - Bepaalde behandelingen bij hormoonstoornissen of sommige kankers. - Enkele antibiotica die op peptiden gebaseerd zijn.

docs.title: Wat betekent dat in de praktijk?
docs.text:
Deze medicijnen helpen bij het beter onder controle krijgen van ziekten (vooral diabetes en overgewicht) en verminderen vaak risico’s op hart- en vaatziekten, nierproblemen en andere complicaties. Ze zijn geen wondermiddel: gezonde voeding, beweging en leefstijl blijven belangrijk. Er kunnen bijwerkingen zijn (bij de GLP-1-spuitjes vaak misselijkheid in het begin).

Let op: de “research peptides” die je online ziet (voor spieren, herstel of anti-aging) zijn meestal niet goedgekeurd, weinig wetenschappelijk bewezen bij mensen en kunnen risico’s hebben. Dat is iets anders dan de echte medicijnen die de huisarts of specialist voorschrijft.

Kortom: peptiden zijn natuurlijke boodschappers in je lichaam. Artsen gebruiken nagemaakte versies daarvan als krachtige, gerichte medicijnen, vooral bij diabetes, overgewicht en een aantal andere aandoeningen. Het werkt het beste in combinatie met leefstijl en onder medische begeleiding.

Dit is algemene uitleg, geen medisch advies. Overleg altijd met je huisarts of specialist wat voor jou geschikt is.
